name: Shop & inventory grid
oneLiner: A modal shop window: buy and sell lists with icons, prices and an amount picker, a bag grid with stacks, a max stack and a capacity, tooltips, and green up / red down arrows comparing gear against what each party member wears. "Not enough gold." and "Your bag is full." are refused with a message, never with negative gold; items sell back at a ratio; Use and Equip call the game's own callbacks. Items and stock are plain objects the designer edits; gold, equipment and stats stay in the game. 16x16 item icons are drawn procedurally. Under autoplay it buys one deterministic upgrade and leaves.
fits: top-down adventure and RPG (a merchant you talk to, a shop tile)
turn-based RPG (a shop between battles or waves, items used through the battle's own item command)
tactics RPG (a shop on the world map between chapters)
action or platformer games with a hub shop
roguelites (a shop room with limited stock)
an inventory screen on its own (bag only: use and equip)
notFor: real-money stores or anything with payment
crafting, item enchanting or random loot rolls (the item table is fixed data)
grid-packing bags where items take several cells

needs: the moment the shop opens (talking to a merchant, a shop tile, a menu key), in update logic: open({stock, onClose})
the game's gold: getGold() and setGold(n), the only way the shop changes it
party members and what they wear: getParty() -> [{id, name}], getEquipped(id, slot) -> item id
apply callbacks: onEquip(id, item, slot, old) recomputes stats; onUse(item, id) applies an effect (false = no effect)
input routed to the shop while busy() (key(code, down) or press(name), tap(x, y)) and the world paused
a fixed 60 Hz update step (the shop's only clock), also while the world is paused
the play field size in native px and ui rects to keep visible (HUD, party panel)
provides: busy flag: route input here and pause the world while the window is open
the bag (module-owned): count / add / remove / setCount / room, for the game's own item command and HUD
serialize() / restore(data): plain JSON for a save file (works inside a save-slots serialize())
onClose({bought, sold, used, equipped, spent, earned, gold, auto}) (synchronous, inside update())
per-action hooks onBuy / onSell / onItems and sound cue names (onSfx)
drawIcon(ctx, kind, x, y): the 16x16 item icons for the game's own menus
the window rectangle on screen, for other overlays

params.label: Where the shop opens (required; the designer's words)
params.default: a merchant the hero talks to

params.label: Window colour (a blue, n slate, b red)

variants.name: Quick shop (one at a time, no prompts)

assets: module/shop-inventory.js: the element as one dependency-free script (global GameDNA_ShopInventory): item table, bag with stacks and capacity, buy / sell / use / equip with checks, comparison, autopilot, serialize / restore, drawing with the 6x8 font and 19 procedural 16x16 icons built in
no image or audio files (sounds are a callback; the game plays its own)
